rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi takes the wording as singling these prophets out for guidance; otherwise the specification would serve no purpose if every accountable person were guided.
rows.anchor: قوله : { هدى الله } دليل على أنهم مخصوصون بالهدى

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi defines following as a later person doing what an earlier person did because the earlier person did it.
rows.anchor: الاقتداء في اللغة إتيان الثاني بمثل فعل الأول لأجل أنه فعله

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī, transmitted by al-Liḥyānī, reports the idiom لي بك قدوة in two vocal forms of قدوة.
rows.anchor: روى اللحياني عن الكسائي أنه قال : يقال لي بك قدوة وقدوة

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads اقتده with kasra on the dāl and a hinted kasra on the hāʾ without a full yāʾ.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر { اقتده } بكسر الدال وبشم الهاء للكسر من غير بلوغ ياء

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisāʾī drop the hāʾ in connected recitation and retain it at pauses; the other readers retain it in both positions.
rows.anchor: والباقون { اقتده } ساكنة الهاء

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī prefers retaining the hāʾ at a pause but dropping it in connection, since it marks pausing like hamzat al-waṣl marks beginning; some retain it in connection to match the written muṣḥaf.
rows.anchor: الوجه الإثبات في الوقف والحذف في الوصل

rows.speaker: أبو بكر ومجاهد
rows.claim: Abū Bakr and Mujāhid call Ibn ʿĀmir's reading wrong because the hāʾ marks a pause and is not inflected; it only exposes the preceding vowel.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر ومجاهد : هذا غلط

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī rejects the charge of error: the hāʾ can stand for the verbal noun, with الاقتداء understood from the verb; it should be still at a pause.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي : ليس بغلط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet refuses payment in imitation of earlier prophets, whose guidance included conveying religion and the law without asking a wage.
rows.anchor: وكان من جملة هداهم ترك طلب الأجر في إيصال الدين وإبلاغ الشريعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān is a reminder containing what people need for worldly life and the afterlife, and the verse implies that Muhammad was sent to everyone in the world.
rows.anchor: يدل على أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم مبعوث إلى كل أهل الدنيا لا إلى قوم دون قوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition follows the permission of slaughter in God's name and includes carrion and animals slaughtered in the name of idols, refuting the polytheists.
rows.anchor: المقصود منه إبطال ما ذكره المشركون

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ applies the verse generally: any food or drink over which God's name was not mentioned is forbidden.
rows.anchor: كل ما لم يذكر عليه اسم الله من طعام أو شراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other jurists unanimously restrict the general wording to slaughter, then differ over whether omission of the invocation makes the meat unlawful.
rows.anchor: أجمعوا على تخصيص هذا العموم بالذبح

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Mālik considers meat unlawful if God's name was omitted at slaughter, whether deliberately or forgetfully.
rows.anchor: كل ذبح لم يذكر عليه اسم الله فهو حرام

rows.speaker: ابن سيرين وطائفة من المتكلمين
rows.claim: Ibn Sīrīn and a group of theologians share Mālik's ruling that omission of the invocation makes slaughter unlawful, whether intentional or forgetful.
rows.anchor: وهو قول ابن سيرين وطائفة من المتكلمين

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa forbids meat when the invocation was deliberately omitted but permits it when omitted forgetfully.
rows.anchor: إن ترك الذكر عمدا حرم ، وإن ترك نسيانا حل

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī permits meat slaughtered by a qualified slaughterer whether the invocation was omitted deliberately or by mistake.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي رحمه الله تعالى : يحل متروك التسمية سواء ترك عمدا أو خطأ إذا كان الذابح أهلا للذبح

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī reads the ban as applying specifically to slaughter in the name of idols, since the verse's final clauses constrain its initially general wording.
rows.anchor: قال الشافعي رحمه الله تعالى : هذا النهي مخصوص بما إذا ذبح على اسم النصب

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī argues that calling the act sinful cannot refer to a Muslim's slaughter when he forgets the invocation, which Muslims do not deem sinful.
rows.anchor: وأجمع المسلمون على أنه لا يفسق أكل ذبيحة المسلم الذي ترك التسمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dispute over what people may eat concerns carrion: polytheists objected that Muslims eat animals killed by hawks or dogs but refuse what God kills.
rows.anchor: ما يقتله الصقر والكلب تأكلونه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports the polytheists' challenge: Muslims eat what they kill themselves but not what God kills.
rows.anchor: تأكلون ما تقتلونه ولا تأكلون ما يقتله الله

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī takes the warning that obedience would make Muslims polytheists as referring to accepting an animal sacrificed in the name of the idols' divinity.
rows.anchor: الذبيحة التي ذبحت على اسم إلهية الأوثان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī's reading is reinforced by 6:145, where the sinful sacrifice is explained as one dedicated to other than God.
rows.anchor: وهو قوله : { قل لا أجد * فيما * أوحى إليك * محرما على طاعم يطعمه إلا أن يكون ميتة أو دما مسفوحا أو لحم خنزير فإنه رجس أو فسقا أهل }

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report says God's remembrance accompanies a Muslim whether or not he utters it; Rāzī understands this as remembrance in the heart.
rows.anchor: ما روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : ( ذكر الله مع المسلم سواء قال أو لم يقل )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if one proof implies prohibition, the permissive evidence prevails because foods are originally lawful and general verses allow eating, use, and good things.
rows.anchor: وجب أن يكون الراجح هو الحل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The prohibition on wasting property also supports permitting the food, since people naturally desire it and it is property.
rows.anchor: لأنه مال لأن الطبع يميل إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite the arguments for permission, a Muslim is better advised to avoid the meat because the text's apparent meaning is strong.
rows.anchor: الأولى بالمسلم أن يحترز عنه لأن ظاهر هذا النص قوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “it is sin” may refer to the act of eating, since the verb implies its verbal noun.
rows.anchor: لأن الفعل يدل على المصدر ، فهذا الضمير عائد إلى هذا المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the uninvoked animal itself is rhetorically called sin, as though it were inherently sinful.
rows.anchor: ما لم يذكر اسم الله عليه في نفسه فسقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation takes the devils as Iblīs and his hosts, who prompted their polytheist allies to dispute with Muhammad and his Companions about carrion.
rows.anchor: المراد من الشياطين ههنا إبليس وجنوده

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima identifies the devils as rebellious Magians who prompted Quraysh polytheists to dispute after hearing the carrion ban and receiving a letter from Persia.
rows.anchor: قال عكرمة : وإن الشياطين ، يعني مردة المجوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Magians' letter argued that Muhammad's followers claim to obey God but deem their own slaughter lawful and what God kills unlawful; the dispute troubled some Muslims and occasioned the verse.
rows.anchor: كتبوا إلى قريش وكانت بينهم مكاتبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After establishing divine oneness, rebutting denials of providence, and rejecting pre-Islamic errors, God commands the Prophet to conclude that his Lord guided him; guidance comes only from God.
rows.anchor: أمره أن يختم الكلام بقوله : { إننى هدانى ربى إلى صراط مستقيم } وذلك يدل على أن الهداية لا تحصل إلا بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative ديناً may be an apposition to the syntactic position of صراط, as in 48:2, “guide you to a straight path.”
rows.anchor: على البدل من محل صراط لأن معناه هداني ربي صراطا مستقيما كما قال : { ويهديك صراطا مستقيما }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the syntax supplies an imperative: “adhere to a religion.”
rows.anchor: أن يكون التقدير الزموا دينا

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: The author of al-Kashshāf says قيماً follows the pattern فَيْعل from قام, like سيد from ساد, and is stronger in meaning than قائم.
rows.anchor: فيما قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) القيم فيعل من قام كسيد من ساد وهو أبلغ من القائم

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة
rows.claim: The Kufans read قيماً with kasra on the qāf and a light yāʾ; al-Zajjāj treats it as a verbal noun like صغر and كبر, meaning a religion endowed with upright values, expressed emphatically.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أهل الكوفة قيما مكسورة القاف خفيفة الياء قال الزجاج : هو مصدر بمعنى القيام كالصغر والكبر والحول والشبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ملة is an apposition to ديناً قيماً, while حنيفاً describes Abraham in the circumstantial accusative; the phrase means God taught him Abraham's monotheistic creed.
rows.anchor: فقوله : { ملة } بدل من قوله : { دينا قيما } وحينفا منصوب على الحال من إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Abraham no polytheist answers the polytheists.
rows.anchor: والمقصود منه الرد على المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblīs attributes his misguidance to God here but says in 38:82 that he himself will lead people astray; Rāzī says this suggests confusion between compulsion and human agency, or that Iblīs treated himself as a proximate misguider and God as the ultimate cause to avoid an infinite regress.
rows.anchor: قول إبليس : { فيما * أغويتنى } يدل على أنه أضاف إغواءه إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Rāzī's theologians define misguidance as placing error, meaning false belief, in the heart; this implies that God creates true and false beliefs in hearts.
rows.anchor: الإغواء إيقاع الغي في القلب

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilites offer two approaches; their first accepts the definition of error as false belief and then gives several replies to Iblīs's attribution of it to God.
rows.anchor: أما المعتزلة فلهم ههنا مقامان

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: Their first reply is that Iblīs's own statement is no proof, even if he believed God creates error, ignorance, and unbelief.
rows.anchor: هذا قول إبليس فهب أن إبليس اعتقد

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: They also say Iblīs could attribute error to God because it appeared after the command to prostrate to Adam, as one may say “do not make me strike you.”
rows.anchor: لما أمر بالسجود لآدم فعند ذلك ظهر غيه وكفره

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: Another reply reads his words as saying that God's curse because of Adam led him to sit in hostility and whisper to people.
rows.anchor: إنك بما لعنتني بسبب آدم فإنا لأجل هذه العداوة ألقى الوساوس في قلوبهم

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: A further reply takes “misguided me” to mean God deprived him of Paradise as punishment for his deed, so he would waylay people.
rows.anchor: قال رب بمآ أغويتنى * لاقعدن لهم

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilite alternative defines igwāʾ as destruction, supported by 19:59 and 11:34 and the idiom for a young camel drinking enough milk to ruin its belly and approach death.
rows.anchor: الوجه الثاني : في تفسير الإغواء الإهلاك ومنه قوله تعالى : { فسوق * يلقون غيا }

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: On this reading, “if God intends to misguide you” in 11:34 means that He intends to destroy you for defiant opposition.
rows.anchor: إن كان الله يريد أن يهلككم بعنادكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī does not rely on Iblīs's statement to prove that misguidance here means error; he argues independently that God misguides Iblīs, since every deviation requires a misguider and the only possible ultimate source is God.
rows.anchor: لا بد له من مغو ، كما أن المتحرك لا بد له من محرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis makes the bāʾ an oath: “by Your power and sovereign rule, I will sit on their straight path to Paradise,” beautifying falsehood and sin; the following lām answers the oath and ما is a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: إنه باء القسم أي بإغوائك إياي لأقعدن لهم صراطك المستقيم أي ، بقدرتك علي ونفاذ سلطانك في

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second analysis takes the phrase causally: because God misled him, Iblīs will in turn strive to mislead them.
rows.anchor: فبسبب إغوائك إياي لأقعدن لهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A third analysis makes ما interrogative—“by what did You mislead me?”—then starts a new clause; Rāzī objects that retaining alif after a preposition with interrogative ما is rare.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : { ما } في قوله : { فيما * أغويتنى } للاستفهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians agree that على is omitted in “I will sit on their straight path”; al-Zajjāj's example shows the preposition can be dropped because the path functions adverbially as a place or time does.
rows.anchor: لا خلاف بين النحويين أن ( على ) محذوف والتقدير : لأقعدن لهم على صراطك المستقيم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj illustrates the omitted preposition with “Zayd struck the back and belly,” meaning he struck on the back and belly.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : مثاله قولك ضرب زيد الظهر والبطن والمعنى على الظهر والبطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Sitting” on the path means persistent, uninterrupted corruption: Iblīs remains at his post whispering without pause.
rows.anchor: المراد منه أنه يواظب على الإفساد مواطبة لا يفتر عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows Iblīs knew the true religion because he calls it God's straight path.
rows.anchor: وصراط الله المستقيم هو دينه الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī infers that Iblīs knew his own creed was error and opposed the true path; one cannot knowingly choose what one recognizes as false, creating a problem about his unbelief.
rows.anchor: الآية تدل على أن إبليس كان عالما بأن الذي هو عليه من المذهب والاعتقاد هو محض الغواية والضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say Iblīs's unbelief was defiant: knowing his doctrine was error and its opposite true, he denied truth only with his tongue.
rows.anchor: من الناس من قال أن كفر إبليس كفر عناد لا كفر جهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others say his unbelief was ignorance, reading his words as expressing what his opponent claims or what he himself believes.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من قال لا . بل كفره كفر جهل

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Rāzī's school argues that God is not obliged to secure people's welfare: He gave Iblīs a long respite despite knowing most people would follow him, causing grave corruption and unbelief.
rows.anchor: يقتضي حصول المفاسد العظيمة والكفر الكبير

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: The argument also notes that God took away the prophets who call people to faith while leaving Iblīs and the devils to call them to unbelief.
rows.anchor: أمات الأنبياء الذين هم الدعاة للخلق

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says Iblīs's presence makes no difference: only people who would stray even without him are misled by his words, as 37:162–163 indicates.
rows.anchor: فقال الجبائي : إنه لا يختلف الحال بسبب وجوده وعدمه

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī adds that if Iblīs actually misled anyone, his continued existence would be a source of harm.
rows.anchor: ولأنه لو ضل به أحد لكان بقاؤه مفسدة

rows.speaker: أبو هاشم
rows.claim: Abū Hāshim allows that some people are misled by Iblīs; his creation resembles increased appetite, which makes resisting sin harder and can increase reward without coercing anyone.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو هاشم يجوز أن يضل به قوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After reporting the people of the Heights speaking to Hell, Rāzī turns to the people of Hell addressing the people of Paradise.
rows.anchor: أتبعه بذكر ما يقوله أهل النار لأهل الجنة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says that after the people of the Heights entered Paradise, Hell's people asked God to let them see and speak to relatives there; Paradise shifted, Hell's people recognized their kin, but the people of Paradise could not recognize the transformed, dark-faced ones.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : لما صار أصحاب الأعراف إلى الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell's people specifically ask for water because their insides are burning intensely from Hell's heat; the verb “pour out” suggests Paradise is higher than Hell.
rows.anchor: وإنما طلبوا الماء خاصة لشدة ما في بواطنهم من الاحتراق واللهيب بسبب شدة حر جهنم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās's account supports that the people of Hell request water while believing they may receive it.
rows.anchor: ما حكيناه عن ابن عباس يدل على أنهم طلبوا الماء

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qāḍī says they ask in despair because they know their punishment is lasting, though even a hopeless person still asks, like a drowning person clutching foam.
rows.anchor: وقال القاضي : بل مع اليأس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “or from what God provided” is said to mean either fruit or food, and their request indicates extreme thirst and hunger.
rows.anchor: هذا الكلام يدل على حصول العطش الشديد

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Abū al-Dardāʾ reports that hunger is sent upon Hell's people to intensify punishment; they receive thorny food that does not nourish, choking food, boiling water and pus, then ask Paradise's people, Malik, and God for relief, are refused, and finally despair.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء أن الله تعالى يرسل على أهل النار الجوع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās describes the people of Paradise seeing God every Friday and receiving gifts from angels through each of their thousand doors.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : أنه ذكر في صفة أهل الجنة أنهم يرون الله عز وجل كل جمعة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The same report pictures Paradise's emerald trees, golden earth, clothing-like leaves, and seedless fruit whiter than silver, softer than butter, and sweeter than honey.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : أنه ذكر في صفة أهل الجنة

rows.speaker: أبو علي الدقاق
rows.claim: Al-Daqqāq says the Hell-dwellers' afterlife craving for food and drink reflects their worldly appetites: a person dies as he lived and is resurrected as he died.
rows.anchor: في تذكرة الأستاذ أبي علي الدقاق ، فقال الأستاذ : هؤلاء كانت رغبتهم وشهوتهم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reply that God has forbidden water and provision to disbelievers means they are completely frustrated.
rows.anchor: ولا شك أن ذلك يفيد الخيبة التامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading says they played with the religion they claimed to follow and were not serious about it.
rows.anchor: وما كانوا فيه مجدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reading says they made amusement and play into their religion.
rows.anchor: أنهم اتخذوا اللهو واللعب دينا لأنفسهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies them as mocking factions (al-mustahziʾīn al-muqtasimīn).
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما يريد المستهزئين المقتسمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling worldly life a deceiver is figurative: desire for long life, comfort, wealth, and status arises during worldly life and distracts people from religion.
rows.anchor: لأن الحياة الدنيا لا تغر في الحقيقة بل المراد أنه حصل الغرور عند هذه الحياة الدنيا

rows.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد والسدي والأكثرون
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, al-Suddī, and most interpreters take “We forget them” to mean “We abandon them,” as they abandoned deeds for this Day.
rows.anchor: نتركهم في عذابهم كما تركوا العمل للقاء يومهم هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God treats them as one who forgets by leaving them in Hell as they turned away from His signs; “forgetting” their punishment follows their forgetting, like the reciprocal wording in 42:40.
rows.anchor: أن معنى ننساهم كما نسوا أي نعاملهم معاملة من نسي نتركهم في النار كما فعلوا هم في الإعراض بآياتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We forget them” means God does not answer their prayers or show them mercy; the severe punishment follows from their denial of His signs.
rows.anchor: لا يجيب دعاءهم ولا يرحمهم

rows.speaker: النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام
rows.claim: Rāzī links worldly attachment to every affliction, citing the prophetic saying that love of this world is the root of every sin and may lead to unbelief and error.
rows.anchor: كما قال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( حب الدنيا رأس كل خطيئة ) وقد يؤدي حب الدنيا إلى الكفر والضلال
